description: REQ-105's cold-start kill-switch -- the ONLY automated pause/monitoring mechanism this spec builds for loan-default risk, hardened across three separate findings over two iterations (FIND-203, FIND-303, plus this iteration's own re-verified PROP-105h) -- is scoped EXCLUSIVELY to loans where a borrower's successfulOnTimeRepayments === 0 AT ISSUANCE ('a genuine cold-start loan, per this requirement's own definition', behavioral-spec.md:657-661). computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own definition (behavioral-spec.md:601-632) is explicit and total: it counts 'the first n ... loans whose ORIGINATING row had successfulOnTimeRepayments === 0 AT ISSUANCE TIME -- full stop, this is the exact and ONLY definition'. A loan issued to an ESTABLISHED borrower (successfulOnTimeRepayments >= 1) is, by this definition, structurally EXCLUDED from computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own sample, and therefore can NEVER influence evaluateColdStartKillSwitch's paused/not-paused decision, no matter how many established-tier loans subsequently default. Yet REQ-105's own doubling ladder (computeLoanCapUsd = min(maxLoanUsd, firstLoanUsd * 2^n), behavioral-spec.md:566-568) is precisely the mechanism that grows an established borrower's available principal from $0.02 up to the $5.00 ceiling (250x the cold-start size) as its successfulOnTimeRepayments count rises -- exactly the tranche where a default causes the largest real dollar loss to a lender (REQ-101's sumOutstandingPrincipalUsd, behavioral-spec.md:294-304, permanently and irrecoverably reduces that lender's own future available surplus for an unrecovered defaulted principal). The spec's own reputation signal (successfulOnTimeRepayments) is COLONY-WIDE, not lender-specific -- a borrower's track record built up against one lender is fully portable to any other, unrelated lender's own eligibility/sizing decision (REQ-105's ladder input is simply countSuccessfulOnTimeRepayments(loanRows, borrowerId), with no lender-pairing restriction anywhere in REQ-101/102/105). This creates a real, unaddressed 'bust-out'/reputation-laundering risk pattern well-documented in real-world credit-fraud literature: a borrower (or a pair of borrowers colluding, or even one borrower simply repaying diligently for its own benefit) can cheaply build a strong track record via a sequence of small, low-risk, successfully-repaid loans, then strategically default on the single largest loan its now-inflated reputation qualifies it for from a DIFFERENT, unsuspecting lender who has never transacted with it before and is relying purely on the colony-wide reputation count -- and this specific default event is, by construction, INVISIBLE to the only automated risk-monitoring mechanism this feature builds, because that mechanism only ever samples successfulOnTimeRepayments===0 loans. Five spec-review iterations have hardened the cold-start kill-switch's WIRING and enforcement (does the real code call it? is the threshold internally consistent? -- FIND-203/303) but none has asked whether the kill-switch's own SCOPE actually covers the tranche of highest dollar exposure. REQ-102(c)'s single-outstanding-loan rule and the fact that a default permanently blocks further borrowing (until an explicit, not-yet-built write-off/correction) does cap the practical damage to roughly one maximally-sized loan per exploiting borrower before lockout -- so this is not an unbounded drain -- but it remains a genuine, currently undocumented edge case: nowhere in REQ-105/106/109's Edge Cases or Acceptance Criteria is 'an established borrower with a strong track record subsequently defaulting on its largest available loan' considered, monitored, or even acknowledged as an accepted, out-of-scope risk the way this spec carefully documents its OTHER known limitations (e.g. GOJO_SENDER_ID's single-sender assumption, the reconciled-path issued_ms asymmetry, the borrower_-prefix lock-key collision). Every other honestly-disclosed limitation in this document gets an explicit 'THE SYSTEM SHALL document this ... as a genuine limitation' treatment; this one gets none.

evidence.snippet: a 'cold-start loan' is NOT equivalent to 'a borrower's own first-ever loan' ... this recomputation ... is the function's own actual algorithm ... Loan issuance (REQ-106) SHALL call this function ... for ANY loan request where the borrower's OWN successfulOnTimeRepayments === 0 at issuance ... an established borrower's non-cold-start renewal loan is NEVER paused by this mechanism, since the kill-switch's entire purpose is to gate the SPECIFIC hypothesis this requirement's own sizing ladder is testing (zero-reputation issuance), not lending in general.

crossCheck.note: PROP-105a through PROP-105h collectively test the cold-start ladder's sizing, the kill-switch's threshold arithmetic, and (PROP-105h) that the real production code actually calls evaluateColdStartKillSwitch for cold-start requests -- none of these proof obligations test, or even mention, monitoring/pausing behavior for a default among ESTABLISHED (successfulOnTimeRepayments>=1) borrowers, because computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own candidate set structurally excludes them by definition (PROP-105f). No PROP anywhere in the 149-item table addresses risk monitoring for the $0.04-$5.00 loan tranche.
